chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: Hite band's first tour up the Pacific Coast
summary: The first organized band to tour from San Diego to Vancouver and Montana when Sebastian's brought in Ben Pollack.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Then the book says, "Marshal also became a familiar soloist at the after-hour jam sessions which Height's sidemen would hold with the resident musicians in the towns which the band visited and he became known to most of the important jazz musicians of the 1930s as a result." What towns did Height's band go to?

We went everywhere on the Pacific Coast. We were the first band, first organized band, to ever travel up and down the Pacific Coast. That is from Los Angeles or from the confines of San Diego on to Vancouver. Then we went as far over on the northern end as Missoula, Montana, and coming further down, we went into Idaho and Utah and Nevada and that was the extent of our traveling.

No, we only did that when we were out of Sebastian's Cotton Club and one of the other big bands came in to replace us, like in one of the years, I went into the band after McKinney's Cotton Pickers had come there, somewhere around 1930, to play. During that time, Les Height would be out doing extemporaneous jobs. All right, the next time we came out of there, another band came in, Ben Pollack came in and we went up the coast. That's the first time the band went all the way to Vancouver. We played every little hamlet in between Los Angeles and Vancouver, Canada. We played them all.
Do you remember what years that was?
